title: Audit ingest — peek-buffer sharding, cost-aware TTL tiers, and SSO sensitivity mapping
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a multi-pronged audit ingestion enhancement that (1) adds a small in-memory 'peek buffer' to smooth hot bursts into the sharder, (2) implements cost-aware TTL tiers with policy-driven compaction windows, and (3) surfaces SSO/SAML-derived sensitivity annotations into the pipeline so admin controls and RBAC v2 decisions can influence retention and routing.
background: Current audit pipeline experiences periodic bursts from rapid admin UI operations (bulk SSO provisioning, RBAC role syncs) which cause uneven shard pressure and temporary query degradation. Storage costs have grown due to conservative uniform retention policies; we lack a clear hook from identity sources (SSO/SAML) to annotate events with sensitivity levels for differentiated retention. Related infra work exists but is fragmented across prior tickets and ad-hoc scripts.
goals: Reduce shard hotspot spikes by smoothing bursts with an in-memory peek buffer feeding sharder at controlled rates
Cut long-tail storage costs by introducing three TTL tiers (hot-7d, warm-30d, cold-365d) and automated compaction rules
Surface SSO/SAML identity attributes (role, group, org_unit) as event sensitivity labels so retention and access controls can be policy-driven
Integrate retention decisions with RBAC v2 so tenant/admin policy overrides are honored during ingestion
non_goals: Not building a full data lake re-ingest system (out of scope)
Not changing downstream audit query semantics in first iteration
Not replacing long-term archival storage provider
proposal: Add a lightweight peek buffer (configurable per-tenant) in the front of the ingest hot path to absorb bursty traffic for up to 10s, emitting to the sharder at a rate cap based on tenant throughput class. Implement a retention-tiering service that consumes annotated events and writes routing headers (hot/warm/cold) plus compaction metadata. Extend SSO/SAML sync (auth service) to produce sensitivity annotations which the ingest front-end attaches to events. Add policy evaluation in the ingress stage that consults RBAC v2 service for administrator overrides (e.g., 'legal_hold=true' forces hot-tier).
design_notes: Peek buffer kept minimal: ring buffer with backpressure to caller after soft limit; per-tenant config to avoid noisy neighbors
Sharder will accept 'preferred_tier' header; sharder will map to partition key + TTL annotations
TTL tiers map to storage classes (hot=SSD hot, warm=cheap-provisioned, cold=glacier-like) with compaction windows to merge small blobs weekly
SSO sensitivity mapping: SAML assertion attribute mapping configured in admin console -> mapped to sensitivity: {public, internal, restricted, legal_hold}
RBAC v2 interaction: evaluation service returns policy decisions fast-path (<20ms) using local cache; fall back to async enforcement if cache miss
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): Implement peek buffer library and integration tests; add rate cap metrics
Phase 2 (3 wks): Extend ingest schema to carry sensitivity headers; wire SSO/SAML sync to emit mappings; add unit tests
Phase 3 (3 wks): Build retention-tiering service and sharder header handling; implement compaction job skeleton
Phase 4 (2 wks): RBAC v2 policy hook integration, admin console controls for per-tenant overrides
Phase 5 (1 wk): Canary rollout for 10 internal tenants, monitor metrics and iterate
rollout_plan: Deploy peek buffer behind feature flag for internal-only tenants
Enable sensitivity annotations for a single SSO-integrated customer and validate mapping accuracy
Enable retention-tier headers in sharder for internal clusters and measure storage distribution
Gradually open feature flag to more tenants based on observed shard pressure and cost reduction metrics
migration_plan: Existing events keep current retention if no sensitivity header present (backwards compatible)
One-time backfill job to annotate high-value historical events based on admin tags (manual run per-tenant)
Update retention reconciliation job to respect newly attached tier headers and perform compaction accordingly
testing_and_metrics: Track shard QPS and per-shard CPU/mem before/after to verify smoothing effect
Metric: 95th percentile write latency to sharder remains within SLO (<150ms)
Metric: per-tenant storage spend delta (30d) and % of data in hot/warm/cold tiers
E2E test: simulate SAML bulk provisioning events and assert no data loss and no shard overload
Property test: RBAC v2 policy override honored during ingest and audit logs show decision trace
monitoring_alerts: Alert if shard_queue_length increases > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes
Alert if compaction_backlog grows beyond safe threshold (configurable per-cluster)
open_questions: How fine-grained should sensitivity mapping be — map directly from SAML attributes or transform to fixed sensitivity buckets?
What default per-tenant peek buffer sizing should be applied to avoid noisy neighbor issues?
Should legal_hold force infinite retention or a long fixed TTL in the first iteration?
Cost allocation model: charge back cold storage differently per-tenant or show aggregated savings only?
decisions: Peek buffer will be bounded and cause backpressure to client after soft-limit; no unlimited buffering
Sensitivity mapping will translate SAML attributes into 4 fixed buckets to simplify policy enforcement
RBAC v2 local cache required; policy evaluation must be <20ms to avoid ingest path timeouts
Initial TTL tiers: hot=7d, warm=30d, cold=365d — subject to admin override via RBAC policies
